content.summary: Welcome to your reading mission on social networking and online safety. In this module, you will learn how to read texts that offer advice on how to use social media safely. You will also discover how to give effective advice using modal verbs and talk about people and things without naming them directly using indefinite pronouns.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Modal verbs for advice (should, had better, ought to) and indefinite pronouns (everyone, anything, no one).
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Terms related to social media, uploading files, passwords, and digital communication.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts to find specific rules and advice, while skimming for main ideas about online behavior.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short B1 texts about social networking and online safety.
Locate specific advice and rules regarding passwords and profile sharing.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with advice modals and indefinite pronouns.

contextWarmup.prompt: How often do you check your social media feeds or chat with friends online?
options: I constantly check my updates several times a day.
I only check my messages once a week.
I never use social networking websites at all.
contextWarmup.explanation: Checking updates constantly is very common for teenagers using social media today, matching our unit theme.

rules: Should + verb (infinitive): digunakan untuk memberikan saran atau nasihat. Contoh: You should think before you post something online.
Had better + verb (infinitive): memberikan saran yang lebih kuat, biasanya ada konsekuensi negatif jika tidak diikuti. Contoh: You'd better not share your password with anyone.
Ought to + verb (infinitive): memiliki makna serupa dengan should, tapi lebih formal. Contoh: You ought to get him a nice present this year.
Indefinite pronouns dengan -one/-body (everyone, someone, anyone, no one): merujuk pada orang. Contoh: Everyone knows that I love music.
Indefinite pronouns dengan -thing (everything, something, anything, nothing): merujuk pada benda/hal. Contoh: I don't like eating anything that has got meat in it.

All / some / none / any + of them: digunakan untuk merujuk kembali ke kelompok (benda atau orang) yang sudah disebutkan. Contoh: There were 500 people at the party, and some of them were smashing windows.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often put 'to' after 'should' or 'had better', or forget that 'ought' requires 'to' before the infinitive verb.
commonTrap.wrong: You should to change your password.
commonTrap.correct: You should change your password, or you ought to change your password.

content.passageTitle: Smart Tips for Safe Social Networking
paragraphs: Social networking is a fantastic way to connect with friends, share photos, and discover new hobbies. However, using these platforms constantly can sometimes lead to trouble if you are not careful. Everyone loves uploading pictures and updating their status, but you should always think twice before you post something online. If you share private details, you might regret it later when strangers or classmates see them.

To keep your accounts secure, you had better follow a few golden rules. First, never share your password with anyone, not even your best friend. Second, you ought to log out whenever you use a computer at school or in a library. If something goes wrong or you feel uncomfortable with a message online, tell an adult immediately. By taking these simple steps, you can enjoy social media safely without any disasters.

content.summary: Practical guide on writing advice and using indefinite pronouns clearly in social networking contexts.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Giving Advice with Modals
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + should / had better / ought to + base verb
blueprintItems.example: You should check your privacy settings before posting photos online.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Using Indefinite Pronouns
blueprintItems.example: Everyone wants to feel safe when using social media platforms.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Quantifiers with Pronouns
blueprintItems.formula: All / some / none / any + of them + plural verb
blueprintItems.example: There are many online profiles, and none of them look genuine.

mechanicsRules.rule: Indefinite pronouns ending in -one or -body take a singular verb in English.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Everyone know that sharing passwords is dangerous.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Everyone knows that sharing passwords is dangerous.
mechanicsRules.why: Words like everyone, someone, and anybody are grammatically singular.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always use the base form of the verb after modal verbs of advice like should or had better.
mechanicsRules.badExample: You should checked your privacy settings.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: You should check your privacy settings.
mechanicsRules.why: Modals must be followed immediately by an infinitive without 'to'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize the first letter of every new sentence and proper application names.
mechanicsRules.badExample: on instagram, someone sent me a strange link.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: On Instagram, someone sent me a strange link.
mechanicsRules.why: Proper nouns and sentence beginnings require standard capitalization.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Social Networking Advice and Safety

content.summary: In this unit, you will learn how to give advice about social networking using modal verbs such as should, had better, and ought to. Clear pronunciation of modal forms and indefinite pronouns is essential for sounding natural and persuasive.
content.audioGuidance: Pay close attention to weak forms in spoken English. Modal verbs like should and had are often unstressed in fast speech, while content words like passwords, disaster, and regret carry strong stress.

pillars.name: Modal Reduction
pillars.target: Pronouncing should and had better naturally
pillars.explanation: In spoken English, auxiliary and modal verbs are pronounced with weak vowel sounds unless you want to emphasize your point.

pillars.name: Indefinite Pronoun Linking
pillars.target: Linking everyone, someone, and no one smoothly
pillars.explanation: Connect the final consonant sound of the pronoun to the following vowel sound in the sentence to maintain a steady speaking rhythm.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress for Advice
pillars.target: Highlighting the main verb when giving recommendations
pillars.explanation: Place primary stress on the action verb and the object, such as change your password or log out safely.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the primary stress moves based on the word structure, with password stressed on the first syllable and apologise on the second.
Disaster has stress on the middle syllable, whereas constantly places the stress firmly on the first syllable.
Regret is stressed on the second syllable, while the verb upload is stressed on the first syllable.
Attach places stress on the final syllable, while the phrasal verb log out stresses the particle verb root first.

drills.targetText: You should always keep your password secret from everyone.
drills.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd ˈɔːlweɪz kiːp jɔːr ˈpɑːswɜːd ˈsiːkrət frɒm ˈevriwʌn/
drills.focus: Using modal verb should and indefinite pronoun everyone
drills.hint: Keep your voice steady on the modal and stress the word password.

drills.targetText: If you upload that photo now, you might regret it later.
drills.phonetic: /ɪf juː ˌʌpˈləʊd ðæt ˈfəʊtəʊ naʊ, juː maɪt rɪˈɡret ɪt ˈleɪtə/
drills.focus: Conditional structure and vocabulary words upload and regret
drills.hint: Pause slightly after the comma to let your listener process the condition.

drills.targetText: Someone had better apologise for causing this online disaster.
drills.phonetic: /ˈsʌmwʌn hæd ˈbetə əˈpɒlədʒaɪz fɔː ˈkɔːzɪŋ ðɪs ˈɒnlaɪn dɪˈzɑːstə/
drills.focus: Advice structure had better and vocabulary apologise and disaster
drills.hint: Emphasize had better to show strong advice and urgency.

drills.targetText: Make sure you log out and do not attach files from strangers.
drills.phonetic: /meɪk ʃʊə juː lɒɡ aʊt ænd duː nɒt əˈtætʃ faɪlz frɒm ˈstreɪndʒəz/
drills.focus: Imperative instructions and phrasal verb log out
drills.hint: Link log and out together without any pause in between.

practicumQuestions.explanation: Use ought to or should naturally to give thoughtful advice.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Act out this roleplay turn reminding someone about computer safety before leaving.
